newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss uncover vegetable smuggling ring.
newsitem.headline: Swiss uncover vegetable smuggling ring.

text.p: Swiss authorities are closing in on a smuggling operation involving illegal transport of vegetables, the Swiss Federal tariff authority and the Swiss Federal Finance ministry said on Tuesday.
"From 1994 to 1996, various firms smuggled 2,165 tonnes of vegetables worth an estimated three million Swiss francs ($2 million) from Italy into Switzerland," the authorities said.
The smuggling operation involved 15 Swiss vegetable wholesale firms, four Italian suppliers and a large cold storage transport firm.
"Investigations are near completion. Import restrictions and duty regulations were violated," authorities said.
Vegetables involved included pototatoes, carrots, tomatoes, beans, onions, endive, cauliflower and leeks. In some cases they were falsely labeled as oranges or lemons, which attract much less duty.
